sample_prep.title: Sample Preparation
sample_prep.description: Welcome to sample prep, where your experiment begins. Keep sample handling consistent across conditions so downstream comparisons stay trustworthy.
sample_prep.objective: Prepare infected and control samples with consistent handling so they are LC-MS ready.
sample_prep.expectations: Understand contamination risks, labeling strategies, and why consistent prep reduces technical bias.

statusMessages.entered: Gloves on, chaos off. Let us prepare our samples like professionals.
statusMessages.success: Sample prep aced. Pipettes are leaving the building.
statusMessages.failed: The tubes are judging us. Try the prep again.

mass_spec.title: Mass Spectrometer
mass_spec.description: Welcome to the mass spectrometer, where peptides become spectra. Robust acquisition settings help getting good identifications.

requires.message: ⚠️ Nice try. The mass spec refuses to run on unprepared samples and pure optimism. Do sample prep first.

mass_spec.objective: Run DDA acquisition and verify spectra quality before downstream processing.
mass_spec.expectations: Understand precursor selection and fragmentation concepts, basic instrument settings, and signs of a successful run.

statusMessages.entered: The mass spectrometer is awake and waiting for peptides.
statusMessages.success: Spectra acquired with smoke coming out of the machine due to its high throughput.
statusMessages.failed: The machine coughed politely. Please rerun.

spectral_search.title: Spectral Search Station
spectral_search.description: Welcome to spectral search, where raw spectra meet protein databases. Tune tolerances and enzyme rules carefully to improve confident matches.

requires.message: ⚠️ Spectral search is locked. The mass spectrometer must run first, or you are searching for peptides in pure imagination.

parameters.label: Search Tool
parameters.tooltip: Search engines differ in scoring models and feature support.

parameters.label: Match Between Runs
parameters.tooltip: Match-between-runs transfers identifications across LC-MS runs. It can improve coverage, but may also propagate incorrect matches if retention alignment is poor.

parameters.label: Precursor Mass Tolerance (ppm)
parameters.tooltip: Lower precursor tolerance is stricter and reduces false matches when mass accuracy is good. Wider tolerance can recover more IDs on noisier data but risks more ambiguity.

parameters.label: Fragment Mass Tolerance
parameters.tooltip: Fragment tolerance controls how closely fragment peaks must align. Tight windows increase specificity for high-resolution MS/MS, while wider windows are more forgiving but less selective.

parameters.label: Enzyme
parameters.tooltip: Enzyme specificity defines expected peptide boundaries. Stricter cleavage rules can improve confidence but may miss real semi-specific peptides in messy samples.

parameters.label: Missed Cleavages
parameters.tooltip: Allowed missed cleavages model incomplete digestion. Higher values increase search space and sensitivity, but can raise computational cost and false discovery risk.

parameters.label: Minimum Peptide Length
parameters.tooltip: Short peptides can be less unique and harder to identify confidently. Raising the minimum length often improves specificity at the cost of some sensitivity.

parameters.label: Maximum Peptide Length
parameters.tooltip: Long peptide allowances influence search scope. Higher maxima can capture rare long peptides, but usually expand search complexity with limited practical gain.

spectral_search.objective: Configure database-search parameters to maximize confident peptide-spectrum matches.
spectral_search.expectations: Understand mass tolerances, enzyme specificity, and trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity.

statusMessages.entered: Time to play hide-and-seek with peptides.
statusMessages.submitting: Interrogating spectra under a bright lamp...
statusMessages.success: Many peptides found. The database search engine breathes exhausted from the vast search space.
statusMessages.failed: No solid alibi from these spectra. Tweak and retry.

filtering.title: Filtering Station
filtering.description: Welcome to filtering, where signal is separated from noise. While strict enough thresholds improve reliability, over-filtering can hide biology.

requires.message: ⚠️ Filtering station is locked until spectral search has produced real protein data. Right now you are filtering pure optimism.

parameters.label: Maximum Number of Missing Values per Protein
parameters.tooltip: This threshold removes proteins with excessive missing values. Lower limits are stricter and improve robustness, while higher limits retain coverage but can increase noise.

parameters.label: Minimum Peptides per Protein
parameters.tooltip: Minimum peptide support controls protein-level confidence. Requiring more peptides reduces questionable IDs but may remove low-abundance true proteins.

filtering.objective: Remove low-confidence identifications without discarding biologically relevant proteins.
filtering.expectations: Understand missing-value behavior, peptide support thresholds, and false-positive control.

statusMessages.entered: Welcome to Protein Bouncer Club. IDs and visa please.
statusMessages.success: Cleaned house. Are the rowdy proteins gone?
statusMessages.failed: Too many rowdy proteins snuck in. Adjust filters.

transform.title: Transform Station
transform.description: Welcome to the transform station, where raw intensities become analysis-ready values. Logarithmic transformations can reduce skew and stabilize variance.

requires.message: ⚠️ Transform station is offline until spectral search has produced actual data. Right now you are trying to normalize a rumor.

parameters.label: Transform Method
parameters.tooltip: Log transforms stabilize variance and reduce right-skewed intensity distributions.

transform.objective: Apply an intensity transformation that stabilizes variance for fair comparisons.
transform.expectations: Understand why log transforms reduce skew and how transformation affects downstream statistics.

statusMessages.entered: Bending numbers to tame the variance.
statusMessages.success: Numbers feel like the have undergone a transformation.
statusMessages.failed: Math yoga cramp. Something went wrong.

normalize.title: Normalize Station
normalize.description: Welcome to normalization, where samples are brought onto a common scale. Pick a method that removes technical drift without erasing valuable information.

requires.message: ⚠️ Normalization is unavailable until spectral search has produced data worth rescuing. At the moment you are standardizing empty ambition.

parameters.label: Normalization Method
parameters.tooltip: Normalization corrects technical shifts between samples. Simple methods (median, total intensity) are robust and easy to understand, while more complex methods (VSN, quantile) can better handle certain data structures but risk overfitting and removing real biological variation if not used carefully.

normalize.objective: Normalize sample intensities to reduce technical shifts while preserving biological signal.
normalize.expectations: Understand batch and loading effects and how normalization methods change comparability.

statusMessages.entered: Normalization lab open. Time to tame sample loading effects.
statusMessages.success: Normalization complete. The samples are finally on speaking terms.
statusMessages.failed: Normalization drift detected. Try another method and rerun.

imputer.title: Imputer Station
imputer.description: Welcome to imputation, where missing values get estimated values. Choose a method that fits your missingness pattern to avoid biased conclusions.

requires.message: ⚠️ Imputation cannot begin until spectral search has produced something missing in the first place. Right now you are repairing imaginary gaps.

parameters.label: Imputation Method
parameters.tooltip: Imputation fills missing values to enable downstream statistics. Simpler methods are stable baselines, while model-based methods can preserve structure but risk introducing assumptions and bias.

imputer.objective: Handle missing values using an imputation strategy appropriate to the dataset structure.
imputer.expectations: Understand missingness mechanisms and how imputation can introduce bias.

statusMessages.entered: Filling in blanks like a magician.
statusMessages.submitting: Summoning missing values from the data ether...
statusMessages.success: Missing values patched. Does it hold up?
statusMessages.failed: The ghosts of NaN remain. Try another method.

multiple_testing_corrector.title: Multiple Testing Corrector
multiple_testing_corrector.description: Welcome to multiple-testing correction, where false positives are kept in check. FDR-based methods usually balance discovery and reliability.

requires.message: ⚠️ Multiple-testing correction is locked until spectral search produces real data. Right now you are adjusting p-values for imaginary proteins.

parameters.label: Multiple Testing Correction
parameters.tooltip: Multiple-testing correction controls false positives across thousands of hypotheses. FDR methods (BH, Storey) usually balance discovery and rigor better than very conservative family-wise controls.

multiple_testing_corrector.objective: Apply multiple-testing correction to control false discoveries across many hypotheses.
multiple_testing_corrector.expectations: Understand adjusted p-values, FDR control, and why correction is required in omics-scale testing.

statusMessages.entered: You will keep false positives on a short leash.
statusMessages.success: False discoveries contained. Statistical order restored.
statusMessages.failed: P-values started a rebellion. Change correction method.

the_cutter.title: The Cutter
the_cutter.description: Welcome to The Cutter, where final candidates are selected. Combine fold-change and adjusted p-value cutoffs for a balanced shortlist.

requires.message: ⚠️ The cutter remains sheathed until spectral search and downstream analysis have produced something worth slicing. Right now you are applying thresholds to wishful thinking.

parameters.label: Fold-Change Cutoff (log2 scale)
parameters.tooltip: Higher fold-change cutoffs prioritize larger biological effects but reduce hit counts. Lower cutoffs retain subtle changes but may include weaker candidates.

parameters.label: Adjusted p-value (FDR) Cutoff
parameters.tooltip: The adjusted p-value threshold sets statistical stringency after correction. Lower values reduce false discoveries but can miss weaker true effects.

the_cutter.objective: Set fold-change and adjusted p-value cutoffs to define a robust candidate list.
the_cutter.expectations: Understand effect-size versus significance trade-offs and threshold impact on hit confidence.

statusMessages.success: Cuts made cleanly. Candidate list looks sharp.
statusMessages.failed: Snipped too wild. Recalibrate those cutoffs.

statistical_analysis.title: Statistical Analysis
statistical_analysis.description: Welcome to statistical analysis, where hypotheses face the data. Choose tests that match your design and data distribution assumptions.

requires.message: ⚠️ Statistical analysis is unavailable until spectral search has produced data worth interrogating. At the moment you are testing hypotheses against fog.

parameters.label: Statistical Test
parameters.tooltip: Choose a test based on distribution assumptions and sample size. Welch is a robust default for unequal variances; non-parametric or permutation approaches can be safer for non-normal data.

statistical_analysis.objective: Choose and run an appropriate statistical test to detect regulated proteins.
statistical_analysis.expectations: Understand test assumptions, group comparison design, and interpretation of significance outputs.

statusMessages.entered: Stats alarm. Interrogate the data with hard questions.
statusMessages.submitting: Running tests while pretending this is fun...
statusMessages.failed: Statistics said nope. Try another test setup.

final_report.objective: Submit your final interpretation report and lock in the emergency action plan before the panic spreadsheet updates again.
